label: Jurisdiction
blurb: How much of the EBSA lies on the high seas, beyond national jurisdiction, and whose waters hold the rest.

headlines.label: Area on the high seas
headlines.note: This is the part of the EBSA beyond every EEZ, where an area-based management tool under the BBNJ Agreement could apply.

headlines.label: EBSA area
headlines.note: The area is the sum of the EBSA's res-6 cells.

charts.title: Share of the EBSA by zone
charts.subtitle: Each cell in an EEZ counts for that EEZ's sovereign state, so overseas territories count for their sovereign.

method: The EBSA's H3 res-6 cells (about 36 km² each, from the res-8 hex) joined to EEZ v12 (Marine Regions). A cell in an EEZ takes the EEZ's primary sovereign (ISO_SOV1); joint regimes and overlapping claims count for the first-listed sovereign only. A cell in no EEZ counts as high seas when it lies within two res-4 rings of the World High Seas v2 mask, or north of 86°N, where the res-4 mask has a gap at the pole. The rest is shown as 'Outside any EEZ': land, estuaries and inland seas such as the Caspian, which EEZ v12 does not cover. A cell on an EEZ boundary counts for the EEZ.
